findings.finding: The epic justifies the whole architecture from the embedding/vector stratum and AC2/AC4 require similar-ticket surfacing on the production `create` path, but the only embedding model on the table (Amazon Titan, named in the first child) is not entitled on the production Bedrock role — iam_s7.tf grants bedrock:InvokeModel only to anthropic.claude-* ARNs — and the epic never records that selecting an unentitled embedding model obliges an infra entitlement change before the production path can satisfy AC2/AC4. The child resolves Titan access for the offline eval only ('a one-off offline eval, not a production path').
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC2/AC4; Constraints ('Model calls are bounded and off the write path'); Child decomposition ('Index and create-time surfacing')
scenarios: ADR selects a Titan-embedding architecture on offline-eval recall; the index-and-surfacing child then cannot embed on the production role, so the create-time vector tier is permanently degraded to lexical-only in production and AC2's vector justification is undeliverable without an un-planned infra change
findings.suggested_fix: Add a constraint to the epic: 'The ADR's embedding-model selection must have a production entitlement path. The current instance role (iam_s7.tf) is scoped to anthropic.claude-* only; if the ADR selects Titan or any other non-Claude embedding model, the index-and-surfacing child must add the corresponding Bedrock ARN to infra before AC2/AC4 can be met in production, and that infra change is a named prerequisite of that child.'

findings.finding: The epic depends on a new Bedrock embedding integration whose auth entitlement is CONTRADICTED by the deployed environment, and the epic text never states this precondition. The production read-phase catch-up path (AC4) and the warm-index create path (AC2) must embed ticket summaries via Bedrock InvokeModel, but infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf (sid ConverseAnthropicClaudeOnly) scopes bedrock:InvokeModel to arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-* and the matching inference-profile ARNs ONLY — no embedding/Titan model ARN is granted anywhere in infra/, so an embedding call from the deployed instance role returns AccessDeniedException. The epic's Failure-disposition bullet mentions an 'embedding surface is unavailable' degraded case but does not record that the embedding integration is UNENTITLED today, nor that resolving it for the production path (not just the offline eval) requires adding an embedding-model ARN to the instance-role grant.
findings.location: Constraints section ('Model calls are bounded...'; 'Failure disposition is advisory-degrades-never-blocks') and AC2 / AC4
scenarios: Implementation child (index + create-time surfacing) ships, warm-index AC2 and cold-catch-up AC4 try to embed on the deployed Gerrit instance role, and every embedding call fails AccessDeniedException — so production silently degrades to the lexical tier the epic set out to beat, while the offline eval passed
An ADR candidate selects Titan embeddings based on the offline-eval entitlement and no one adds the production ARN grant before the implementation children land
findings.suggested_fix: Add a precondition bullet: the chosen embedding model's Bedrock ARN must be added to the gerrit-instance-role grant in infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf before the index/create-time child can embed in production; until then the create path serves the lexical tier. The first child's developer-identity entitlement covers only the offline benchmark.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the constraints and AC1, state per degraded arm (embedding-surface-down, catch-up/rebuild-fails, judge-errors) whether the degradation is transient/recoverable-on-next-read or permanent-for-this-call, using an explicit disposition word, so the ADR's 'which tier serves each degraded case' also fixes recoverability.
evidence: 'if the index is missing, catch-up or rebuild fails, the embedding surface is unavailable, or the judge errors, the suggestion field comes back empty or lexical-only with a diagnostic and the create still succeeds. The ADR records which tier serves each degraded case.'

The chain composes ≥2 arms (vector->lexical->empty); the plan states the terminal caller-visible result (empty/lexical, create succeeds) but not, per arm, whether the degradation is permanent-for-this-call vs recoverable-on-next-read with an explicit disposition word.
Advisory criterion errs toward surfacing; the catch-up-fails arm's recoverability is the one disposition the plan leaves to the ADR without a disposition word.
findings.finding: The failure-disposition chain is stated as 'advisory-degrades-never-blocks' with tiers (embedding unavailable -> lexical-only; index/catch-up/rebuild fails -> empty + diagnostic; create always succeeds), and the per-tier disposition is delegated to the ADR, but the plan does not state the disposition of the catch-up-failure arm using an explicit recoverable/permanent word: when a cold read-phase catch-up fails, is the newly-created ticket permanently unfindable for that create (fatal-for-this-call) and recoverable on the next read/batch (retryable-across-calls), or silently dropped?
findings.location: Constraints: 'Failure disposition is advisory-degrades-never-blocks' and AC4 (read-phase catch-up)
scenarios: A cold catch-up throws mid-rebuild on one create: does the next create retry the incremental update, or is the index left in a half-built state that degrades permanently to lexical?
The embedding surface is down for a window of creates: the plan says lexical-only, but does not say this is transient (recovers when the surface returns) vs. latched.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an inline disposition clause: 'Each degraded arm is recoverable, not latched: an embedding-surface outage degrades to lexical-only for the affected creates and recovers automatically when the surface returns; a failed cold catch-up or rebuild leaves the prior index intact (no half-written state) and is retried on the next read, so the new ticket becomes findable then; the judge-error arm returns lexical candidates. In no arm does a non-blocking degradation mask a recoverable condition — create always succeeds and nothing is retried on the write path.'
